stays.name: Grand Hôtel Doré
stays.blurb: Having opened its doors at the beginning of the 20th century The Grand Hotel Doré has been owned and operated by the same family ever since, giving the place plenty of character and quite a bit of ch…

stays.name: Le Citizen Hotel
stays.blurb: To an American, it will feel cramped, but it is well appointed and comfortable.

stays.name: Pullman Paris Bercy
stays.blurb: The former Sofitel was demoted to Pullman, but has since been afforded a thorough renovation (finished in autumn of 2013) to bring it up to current Pullman brand standards along with other Pullman ho…

stays.name: Quality Hotel Gare Du Nord
stays.blurb: Housed in a historic building dating back to 1868, the Quality Hotel includes in all its rooms modem plugs, Wi-Fi access, and tea & coffee makers.

stays.name: AIJ Paris
stays.blurb: Some sites (including their own) says they are a youth-only hostel, but there do not enforce any age restrictions.

stays.name: Hôtel Vicq d'Azir
stays.blurb: This little cheapie is in the process of a renovation under its new management.

activities.title: Bakery and cheese walk
activities.blurb: Croissant, baguette, three cheeses, zero regrets.

activities.title: Falafel in the Marais
activities.blurb: Queue on Rue des Rosiers, eat on the street.

activities.title: Musée d'Orsay
activities.blurb: Impressionists inside an old train station.
activities.wiki: File:Paris - Musée d'Orsay - big clock seen from the interior.jpg

activities.title: Montmartre wander
activities.blurb: Hilltop streets, painters and a view over the rooftops.

activities.title: Picnic on the Seine
activities.blurb: Wine, bread and a riverside spot at golden hour.

activities.title: Eiffel Tower at night
activities.blurb: It sparkles for five minutes every hour after dark.

activities.title: Jazz club in the Latin Quarter
activities.blurb: Cellar club, live band, late night.

activities.title: Versailles day trip
activities.blurb: The palace, the hall of mirrors and huge gardens.

activities.title: Swim at Piscine Molitor
activities.blurb: A stunning classical swimming pool complex.

activities.title: Wine and cheese tasting
activities.blurb: Six wines, five cheeses and how to pair them.

activities.title: Rue Cler market street
activities.blurb: Picnic shopping: cheese, fruit, charcuterie, pastries.
activities.wiki: File:Fruit shop, Rue Cler, Paris 12 April 2011.jpg

activities.title: Louvre highlights
activities.blurb: Mona Lisa, Venus and the glass pyramid. Book a time slot.

activities.title: Sainte-Chapelle stained glass
activities.blurb: A room made almost entirely of glass. Go on a sunny day.

activities.title: Luxembourg Gardens stroll
activities.blurb: Green chairs, toy sailboats and the palace.

activities.title: Shakespeare and Company
activities.blurb: The famous English bookshop facing Notre-Dame.

activities.title: Seine dinner cruise
activities.blurb: Glide past lit-up bridges with a glass of wine.

activities.title: Giverny day trip
activities.blurb: Monet's garden and water lilies, an hour away.

activities.title: Aquaboulevard
activities.blurb: Biggest swimming pool and recreational center inside Paris.

activities.title: Bercy Village
activities.blurb: For a taste of the French countryside, a visit to Bercy Village brings to life the spirit of market shopping inside Paris.

activities.title: L'Astrance
activities.blurb: 3 Michelin stars. Considered one of the best restaurants of Paris.

activities.title: Paris catacombs
activities.blurb: Tunnels lined with millions of bones. Spooky and fascinating.

activities.title: AccorHotels Arena
activities.blurb: An indoor sports arena that seats around 17,000 for sports and slightly over 20,000 for major concerts; formerly known as Palais des Omnisports de Paris-Bercy and Bercy Arena.

activities.title: Jardins du Trocadéro
activities.blurb: Tourists cross this park with the large fountain on the way to the Place du Trocadéro viewpoint to the Eiffel Tower.

activities.title: Bataclan
activities.blurb: Attend a concert or have a drink at this popular café-concert music hall inaugurated in 1865 featuring brightly painted Chinese architecture.

activities.title: Cabaret show
activities.blurb: Feathers, can-can and champagne in Pigalle.

activities.title: Bike tour along the river
activities.blurb: Easy flat ride past the big sights in three hours.

activities.title: Bang!
activities.blurb: Offers a selection of first class meats from all over the world (From American Angus and French Aubrac to Argentine Angus and Simmental from Bavaria), along with natural wines.

activities.title: Julien
activities.blurb: The original 1890 decor of this Parisian dining classic is a mix of Cuban mahogany and Art Nouveau paintings and fixtures - an atmospheric treat.

activities.title: Picpus Cemetery
activities.blurb: A must for anyone interested in the history of the American Revolution.

activities.title: Cimetière de Montparnasse
activities.blurb: The burial place of existentialist philosopher Jean-Paul Sartre, feminist Simone de Beauvoir (both of whom lived nearby); musician Serge Gainsbourg; artist Man Ray; the poets Charles Baudelaire, Guy de Maupassant, Charl…

activities.title: Nouveau Casino et Café Charbon
activities.blurb: The New Casino keeps rocking until dawn both in the bar downstairs and the medium-size dance hall upstairs, making it the favourite among young Parisians, especially after the other places in the neighbourhood have clos…

activities.title: La Fée Verte
activities.blurb: La Fée Verte is an absinthe bar (and café) as it was known more than 100 years ago.

activities.title: Canal Saint-Martin apéro
activities.blurb: Sit on the canal edge with friends and a bottle.

activities.title: Jardin Yitzhak Rabin
activities.blurb: Nestled in the centre of the Parc Bercy (below) is a lovely, and truly peaceful, garden with several waterworks and other high-quality landscape-art pieces.

activities.title: Avé Maria
activities.blurb: Brazilian favela chic. The friendly folks who run this place have been hosting Brasilian dance nights at various venues around town.

activities.title: Soya Cantine Bio
activities.blurb: A true organic, vegetarian restaurant, and a good one.

activities.title: Cité Internationale Universitaire de Paris
activities.blurb: The C.I.U.P. is a student quarter established in 1925, providing homes for about 10,000 students, scientists, and artists from 120 countries.

activities.title: Observatoire
activities.blurb: The observatory was erected by Claude Perrault from 1667 to 1672 by order of Colbert.
activities.address: 61, av de l'Observatoire, entrance: 77, av Denfert-Rochereau

activities.title: Café de l'Homme
activities.blurb: Get a fantastic view of the Eiffel Tower from this restaurant-tearoom opposite the Champ de Mars.

activities.title: Buttes-Chaumont Park
activities.blurb: Popular city escape for nature lovers and walkers who can spend hours wandering around this lush green paradise.

activities.title: Bateau Phare
activities.blurb: This little red lighthouse boat hosts dance and chill electronic music and other multimedia cultured events and has been one of the coolest spots around for some time.

activities.title: Promenade Plantée
activities.blurb: If you were a city planner in one of the great cities of our Earth and you discovered that a railroad right-of-way had been abandoned and would never be used again what might you do?

activities.title: Caffe Panem
activities.blurb: Pasta and bruschetta featured in this small family-run café that serves good and cheap coffee (90 cents for an espresso cup), croissants and great home made sweets such as tiramisu (standard and with chestnut purée).

activities.title: Terra Rosse
activities.blurb: Authentic Italian pizzeria, restaurant and deli, The chef's offerings are very authentic and fresh.

activities.title: Port-Royal Abbey
activities.blurb: Famous people who stayed here include Marie de Rohan, intriguer during the Fronde; Jeanne Baptiste d'Albert de Luynes, future mistress of a duke of Savoy; Marie Angélique de Fontanges, mistress of Louis XIV, died here g…

activities.title: Tour Montparnasse
activities.blurb: If the queues at the Eiffel Tower are just too much for you and your time is limited, consider a trip up the Montparnasse Tower.

activities.title: Le square café
activities.blurb: In spring time sun is shining on the outdoor terrace.

activities.title: Paris By Scooter
activities.blurb: All Vespa scooter rentals and Paris guided City tours include the collect and picked up from, your hotel in Paris.

activities.title: Paris Saint-Germain
activities.blurb: PSG play soccer in the top-tier Ligue 1.
activities.address: Parc des Princes, 24 Rue du Commandant Guilbaud

activities.title: Parc Montsouris
activities.blurb: Considered one of the most colourful Parisian parks, a local favourite, the Parc Montsouris was opened in 1878, having been designed by Alphand for Baron Haussmann.

activities.title: Café Cannibale
activities.blurb: Very chic bar and café with DJ sets weekends; live music Friday and Saturday.

activities.title: Le Café des Anges
activities.blurb: Good variety of French café dishes with a few oriental offerings such as Bõ Bun.

activities.title: Musée Pasteur
activities.blurb: The Pasteur Museum is housed in the apartment where the great scientist spent the last 7 years of his life.

activities.title: Palais de Chaillot
activities.blurb: Great perspective on the Eiffel Tower and Left Bank from Place du Trocadéro in between the two buildings of the palais.

activities.title: Truc Café
activities.blurb: A classic French wine bistro filled with young trendy singles.

activities.title: Boulevard Saint-Germain
activities.blurb: The Boulevard Saint-Germain is a major street in Paris on the Rive Gauche of the Seine.

activities.title: Stade Français
activities.blurb: Rugby club in the Top 14, and a perennial title contender.

activities.title: Bois de Boulogne
activities.blurb: A park along the western edge of the 16ème arrondissement of Paris, near the suburb of Boulogne-Billancourt.

activities.title: Bistro Paul Bert
activities.blurb: A most classic Parisian bistro serving many first-time visitors to Paris and others who return.

activities.title: Les Petits Crus
activities.blurb: Les Petits Crus is a wine bar specializing in a marriage between wine and cheese.

activities.title: Musée Marmottan
activities.blurb: This charming museum is owned by the French Académie des Beaux-Arts.

activities.title: Musée en Herbe
activities.blurb: With a teaching style based on fun and humour, the Musée en Herbe offers classes and games about art especially designed for children.

activities.title: Boulevard du Temple
activities.blurb: The Boulevard du Temple, formerly nicknamed the "Boulevard du Crime", is a thoroughfare in Paris that separates the 3rd arrondissement from the 11th.

activities.title: Boulevard Saint-Michel
activities.blurb: The Boulevard Saint-Michel is one of the two major streets in the Latin Quarter of Paris, France, the other being the Boulevard Saint-Germain.

activities.title: Le Moulin Rouge
activities.blurb: With two shows a night, this turn-of-the-20th century burlesque palace offers a big production choreographed dance show interspersed with comedians, jugglers, and magicians.

activities.title: Bois de Vincennes
activities.blurb: There are many beautiful footpaths, a Buddhist Temple, and a lake with rowboats available for rental (about €10 as of 2009).

activities.title: Le Temps des Cerises
activities.blurb: If you are looking for quality French food and a large choice of good and affordable wine, this is the place to go.

activities.title: Le Volant
activities.blurb: The Basque restaurant excels in meat.

activities.title: Place Pigalle
activities.blurb: The sleaze of boulevard de Clichy between place Pigalle and place Blanche can provide a moment of distraction.

activities.title: Espace Dali
activities.blurb: A fantastic and undeservedly little-known collection of the great surrealist artist's often overlooked sculptural works.

plan.budgetNote: Stay came in $188 over target, so I moved money from flights, which came in $697 under.
